subject.title: [Bug]: /context detail shows ~62k untracked provider/runtime overhead on fresh OpenAI Codex gpt-5.5 session

question: Should `/context detail` grow a provider-aware context ledger for Codex token usage, and which buckets should count toward context-window occupancy versus billing-only usage?
rationale: The current source proves the generic residual label remains, but only maintainers can decide the product semantics for cache, native thread state, hidden provider state, unknown residuals, and compaction thresholds without overpromising provider behavior.

options.title: Define Provider-Aware Ledger
options.body: Keep this issue open, require live Codex OAuth proof, and implement confidence-tagged buckets plus explicit billing/context-window semantics.

options.title: Keep Generic Residual
options.body: Accept the current `Untracked provider/runtime overhead` line as sufficient and close this as not planned after documenting that limitation.

options.title: Repro First Only
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers or a contributor post a current-main Codex run showing the exact residual and raw token fields.

recommendation.title: Define Provider-Aware Ledger
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, require live Codex OAuth proof, and implement confidence-tagged buckets plus explicit billing/context-window semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Codex app-server and usage-accounting history makes steipete the best available owner for the Codex/provider semantics decision.
